description:
Defect: (reduce/2 `:first | {:acc, b}` sentinel) x (Range). The sum-typed accumulator does not thread back through the Range reduce recursion, so the fold returns its initial {:cont, :first} unadvanced and reduce_first_acc(:first) raises Enum.EmptyError (enum.fz:243).

Reproduced on HEAD (`Enum.reduce(1..3, fn (x, acc) -> x * acc end)` / `1..7//2`): runtime panic `Enum.EmptyError` in interp and on the native path alike.

CONFIRMED distinct from f98.6 -- do NOT merge them. Probed on HEAD: reduce/2 over Range publishes ZERO callable boundaries (the reducer dispatches DIRECTLY), so this cannot be the f98.6 published-boundary resolution fragmentation -- there is no boundary to fragment. No transport boundary, no resolution set, no convergence-class / callable-boundary machinery is involved. This break lives in the direct Range-reduce path (Range.reduce_cont / reduce_step threading the accumulator, range.fz:55-68), one layer below the callable-boundary system.

Controls pin the locus exactly (both publish zero boundaries):
- reduce/2 over a LIST works: Enum.reduce([1,3,5,7], fn (x,acc) -> x*acc end) = 105.
- reduce/3 over a RANGE works: Enum.reduce(1..7//2, 0, fn (x,acc) -> x+acc end) = 16.
So the defect is the intersection of the sentinel UNION accumulator (`:first | {:acc, b}`) with the Range reduce path. List.reduce threads the same union correctly; Range threads a plain accumulator correctly; only union x Range fails.

Northstar: the `:first | {:acc, b}` union must round-trip as the threaded accumulator through Range.reduce_cont exactly as it does through List.reduce. Investigate why the union-typed accumulator value is delivered/dispatched wrong on the Range path -- likely a repr or delivery mismatch for the sum-typed accumulator across the (direct) Range reduce recursion -- using the two green controls as regression anchors. Blocks fz_f98_range_reduce2 (bfh.2) run/interp/build.
title: Enum.reduce/2 over Range raises Enum.EmptyError: :first|{:acc} accumulator does not thread through the shared bridge over non-List Enumerables
